name: Investigative Journalism
description: Build a documented investigative reporting project from hypothesis through source verification, evidence matrix, right-of-reply, and publication review.

tasks.name: Frame the investigation
tasks.objective: Define the public-interest question, falsifiable hypotheses, jurisdictions, entities, timelines, known claims, likely records, source classes, conflicts, and what evidence would disprove the working theory.

tasks.name: Build the evidence base
tasks.objective: Collect primary records, datasets, filings, contracts, court or regulatory documents, archived pages, and on-record material. Preserve source URLs, dates, copies, provenance, and chain-of-custody notes.

tasks.name: Interview and corroborate
tasks.objective: Interview knowledgeable sources using non-leading questions. Distinguish firsthand knowledge from hearsay and corroborate consequential claims with independent records or sources.

tasks.name: Construct claim-evidence matrix
tasks.objective: Map every material claim to supporting evidence, contradictory evidence, confidence, unresolved gaps, attribution requirements, and legal or ethical risk.

tasks.name: Run right-of-reply and fact check
tasks.objective: Send precise, evidence-based questions to materially affected subjects with reasonable response opportunity. Re-check names, dates, numbers, quotes, documents, context, and disputed claims.

tasks.name: Prepare publication record
tasks.objective: Produce the story architecture plus source notes, evidence links, uncertainty language, response handling, corrections plan, and a clear boundary between documented fact and interpretation.
